title: Model lifecycle KV stability telemetry and per-segment benchmarking
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: produce a reproducible onboarding playbook that uses per-segment (context-window) benchmarking and stability telemetry to decide model-version pinning and KV retention TTLs. This ticket covers instrumentation, an offline profiling pass across sampled workloads, an automated scoring model (stability_score) for version affinity, and a publishable artifact (segment-level profile + recommended pin/TTL) to be consumed by the onboarder/orchestrator. The work must minimize risk to live traffic (canary-first rollout) and provide clear rollback criteria.
background: Operationally we see large variance in KV hit rate and memory churn across customers and models when sequence-length distributions are heavy-tailed. Existing onboarding exposes single-number recommendations (e.g., retention=30m) that underperform on tail-heavy apps. We need a per-model, per-segment approach: bucket context windows into quantiles (short/medium/long/tail), record warmup curves, and derive TTLs and pinning affinity that optimize under SLO constraints (p95 latency, token-cost).
approach: 1) Instrument: add segment-level telemetry (bucket_id, sample_count, kv_hit_rate, warmup_steps, avg_kv_size) and a deterministic context fingerprint for later deduping. 2) Offline profiler: run sampled traces through a simulator to generate per-segment performance curves for model-version candidates (vX, vY). 3) Scoring: compute stability_score = weighted combination of kv_hit_rate p50..p99, warmup slope, and memory_stddev; produce recommended retention TTL per segment and version-affinity score. 4) Publish: create a segment-profile artifact in profile-store and surface recommendation in the onboarder. 5) Rollout: canary with 1% of traffic, monitor cost/latency regressions, expand to 10% then global if thresholds met.
success_criteria: Per-model segment profile artifact published for at least 50 models in the catalog
Automated recommendation reduces tail p95 latency by >=5% on canary customers or token cost by >=3% without degrading p50
Stability_score correlates with real-world rollback decisions (precision>0.8 in historical replay)
Monitoring dashboards show KV hit-rate improvement for targeted segments within 24h of rollout
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: aggressive TTLs increase memory pressure -> Mitigation: include mem_budget check and clamp TTLs by model pool capacity
Risk: incorrect fingerprint collisions bias profiles -> Mitigation: use 128-bit hash with per-bucket salt and sample verification
Risk: profiling cost -> Mitigation: limit offline simulator runs to sampled traces and amortize across versions using delta-simulations
implementation_notes:
- Telemetry schema: append segment_id, segment_quantile (q0..q3), sample_hash, warmup_steps_vector (compressed), kv_byte_histogram (buckets), version_tag. Keep payload small (<=1KB) and ship via existing metrics pipeline.
- Scoring parameters configurable via /config/kvcache/segment-scoring.json.
- Output artifact format: newline-delimited JSON per segment with fields (segment_quantile, recommended_ttl, version_affinity_score, sample_count, derived_mem_pct).
rollout_plan: Phase A (offline): profile 2000 sampled traces across 5 representative models (2 days). Phase B (canary): publish recommendations for 3 low-risk customers at 1% traffic for 48h. Phase C (scale): expand to 10% then 50% with automated checks. Phase D (global): default recommendation enforced for onboarded versions after 14 days of stable metrics.
rollback_criteria: Immediate rollback if p95 latency regresses >10% or KV evictions increase >15% or host memory saturation risk >5% above baseline. Automated abort if any of the metrics breach for 2 consecutive 10-minute windows.

next_steps: 1) Finalize bucket boundaries with analytics (short/med/long/tail). 2) Merge telemetry proto PR and rollout sampling to 5% across staging. 3) Run full offline profiling on selected models and publish initial artifacts.
notes: Prefer percentiles over means when computing stability to avoid skew from outliers.
We will avoid automatic global enforcement for first two months; recommendations are advisory until confidence thresholds met.
Plan to reuse the profile-store format used by ENG-31137 to ease consumption by the onboarder
